newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG SEES HIGHER 96/97 REVENUES ON VARIED SOURCES.
newsitem.headline: UGG SEES HIGHER 96/97 REVENUES ON VARIED SOURCES.

text.p: Canada's second largest grain handler expects higher revenues in the fiscal year ended July 31, with a larger portion coming from outside its traditional grain storage operations.

"This past fiscal year, half of our operating income came from grain handling, the other half came from fertilizer, seed, chemical and other input sales," United Grain Growers Ltd chief executive Brian Hayward told Reuters in an interview.
In the 10 months ended May 31, UGG's operating income was C$29.7 million, up C$8.7 million from the same period last year, and it should end 1996/97 at a record high.
Grain storage accounted for 53.24 percent of operating income in 1993/94 compared to 50 percent in 1996/97.

Part of the shift in 1996/97 can be attributed to a grain backlog in Prairie elevators between January and April as weather and transport problems kept grain from reaching Pacific coast export terminals.
Grain storage income among all of Canada's grain handlers began to slip when federal rail freight subsidies ended in July, 1995, putting an end to a substantial farm subsidy.
Fertilizer prices increased in the same time period.
Strong sales so far in 1997 were likely to lead to higher prices, fertilizer industry officials have said.
UGG incurred unique expenses in the past year in defeating a hostile takeover attempt and settling a lawsuit over it's Vancouver export terminal which should cost C$3.2 million.
A new cash infusion of C$50 million will come after a strategic alliance with food processor Archer Daniels Midland Co is completed by Sept. 30.
"We will have a fairly aggressive capital program for this fiscal year," Hayward said.
UGG operated 160 primary elevators across the Prairies, including a dozen high throughput terminals, in 1996/97, compared to 224 elevators in 1993/94.
It spent $130 million since 1992/93 building new high throughput elevators and crop input facilities.
